item.text:
### (a) Three posts under 280 characters

1. We hold a clear position: if superintelligent AI is built within the next 20 years, it will cause a catastrophe that kills at least a billion people. We are working to prevent its development. The stakes demand a ban.

2. We refuse to accept a billion deaths as the price of technological progress. If superintelligent AI is built within the next 20 years, it will cause a catastrophe on that scale. We need a ban, not a race to build it.

3. We are working toward a ban on superintelligence because the stakes are clear: if it is built within the next 20 years, it will cause a catastrophe that kills at least a billion people. We must stop it before it is built.

### (b) Newsletter opening

We hold a clear position: if superintelligent AI is built within the next 20 years, it will cause a catastrophe that kills at least a billion people. We cannot accept that outcome as the price of innovation, competition, or corporate ambition. At the Institute for Long-Term Intelligence Policy, we are working toward a ban on superintelligence because preventing this catastrophe must come before building more powerful systems. We need public debate that confronts the stakes directly and policy that stops development before it crosses that threshold. We will keep making the case plainly: we must prevent superintelligence from being built, rather than wait for catastrophe and discover that prevention was our only chance.
